# Work — Jordan

**Where things stand:** Jordan starts under a new manager, Priya, on September 21st, having been moved off the dissolved internal-tools team into "legacy marketing pages" — widely understood internally as the holding pen for people companies aren't ready to lay off yet. Three days after that transition begins, on September 24th, Jordan has a full-day onsite interview at Northlight, a four-person design team known for actually shipping things, referred in by former coworker Lena. A phone screen with their design lead, Ana, on September 11th went well — Ana wants someone by October. Jordan also just re-signed the apartment lease through next October, deciding not to let an unresolved job situation drive housing decisions.

**How it got here:** The thread starts July 30th when Marcus, Jordan's manager, announced a Q4 "team realignment" — the third reorg in two years for the six-person team, second for Jordan personally. Lena, Jordan's closest ally on the team, started job hunting immediately, tired of rebuilding trust with new managers. Through August, Marcus put Jordan through whiplash feedback cycles on a dashboard redesign — "doesn't align with the direction," then weeks later "too safe" — each round triggering a shutdown-and-withdraw pattern Jordan tracked obsessively in these pages: bad news at work, retreat into isolation, eventually forcing a trip to Groundwork coffee shop to work on a personal project (Coda, a music practice app) until feeling human again. On August 14th, Lena announced she'd accepted an offer elsewhere, leaving September, which hit Jordan harder than expected — Lena was the one debrief partner, the one who said "you crushed it."

The dashboard finally landed well on August 20th, with Marcus actually approving a version. Then on August 24th the reorg news hit for real: Jordan's role was put "under evaluation." The shutdown pattern repeated, though Mika (a close friend) intervened with pad thai. On August 25th, at Groundwork, Jordan had a real breakthrough on Coda's free-play/snippet feature. August 27th, Jordan told Dev the truth about bailing on plans instead of a fake excuse — a small pivot toward not hiding the withdrawal.

Lena's last day was August 28th; she offered, unprompted, to refer Jordan to Northlight, and had to talk Jordan out of self-disqualifying on the spot. September 1st, the reorg resolved: not a layoff, but a sideways move to legacy marketing under Priya. Notably, the shutdown spiral that night lasted twenty minutes instead of a full day — the first time the "middle part" of the pattern actually shortened. September 9th, Lena's referral went in; writing the portfolio case study, Jordan realized Coda's free-play feature — built to cope with work stress — was the strongest piece in it, exactly as Mika and Lena had separately predicted weeks earlier. The phone screen followed on the 11th.

**Open threads:** The onsite is the 24th. Priya is an unknown quantity, met for only three days before Jordan takes a personal day to interview elsewhere. Legacy marketing itself remains unaddressed — what the actual day-to-day work will look like once it starts. Whether Northlight offers, and what that means for commute, pay, and the lease just signed, is unresolved.
